waypoints.title: fence FIFO admission: DESIGN the WAIT-line protocol (implementation split to W47)
waypoints.next_bounded_step: None -- this waypoint is done. See W47.
waypoints.evidence: 2026-09-26: 2026-09-26 MEASURED LIVE (W38), scratch ledger under /var/tmp, never the real ledger: fixture TOTAL_MB 100 + a dead LEASE (pid 999999) + WAIT bbbb 8888:1 <epoch> 50 blocked-job. (1) GC KEEPS a WAIT line verbatim: membudget status (which runs ensure then gc under lock) reaped the dead LEASE but left the WAIT line byte-identical, because membudget-ledger's gc() case-matches only 'LEASE *' (membudget-ledger:109) and falls through everything else, WAIT included, to the unconditional keep branch (line 121) — no liveness check ever runs on it, confirmed by the dead WAIT owner (8888:1) surviving. (2) ADMISSION IGNORES it completely: MEMBUDGET_NOBLOCK=1 membudget run 85 probe-job admitted instantly, reporting 'global free was 100MB' — the WAIT line's 50MB was never subtracted. Root cause read at source: _snapshot() (scripts/membudget:105-110) awk-sums only dollar1==TOTAL_MB and dollar1==LEASE; no code path anywhere in cmd_run reads a WAIT line for budget, ordering, or anything else. Conclusion: any WAIT-line design is safe to introduce (gc will carry it) but is COMPLETELY INERT on the bash side until bash's admission is taught to read it — FIFO holds only once both clients honour the line, exactly as queue.md predicted. | 2026-09-26: 2026-09-26 DESIGNED: a Waiter dataclass mirrors Lease's 7-field ledger shape -- WAIT ticket mb owner epoch parent label -- so parse/gc/render reuse the same word-count and liveness machinery leases already have, instead of treating a WAIT line as opaque extra forever. Semantics, chosen after W38's measurement: STRICT head-of-line FIFO, not any-waiter-that-currently-fits -- admission proceeds only when the verdict is ADMIT for this request AND either no live waiters exist or this request's own ticket is the oldest live one, so a later smaller request can never overtake an earlier larger one even when it would itself fit right now. That is exactly the failure summit's witness measured (later arrival B admitted ahead of waiting A) and the only reading of 'arrival-order admission' that actually closes it -- the weaker any-that-fits reading would still starve A behind an endless stream of small Bs. Dead waiters are reaped by gc using the SAME is_alive predicate as leases, no cascade (a waiter has no children). A WAIT line is appended on first BLOCK and removed atomically with either the LEASE append (same locked section) or a terminal refusal/give-up, so no window exists where a ticket is queued but nothing will ever clear it. Split into W47 (implement in admit.py, one commit), W48 (letter to substrate; bash's own side stays inert per W38 until it lands its own patch), W49 (tell summit and amr-skills).

waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-01: inventory measured: 13 distributions, 0 cross-distribution imports (ast over src and tests; positive control 436 same-distribution imports), so all coupling is shared infra (MODULE.bazel 31 hubs, venv.bzl, check drivers, .githooks, 3 cross-package hooks tests, SKELETON/INSTALL). Plan and order in .claude/design/W317-split-plan.md | 2026-10-01: operator ruling 2026-10-01: one-version rule's PURPOSE (agents stay current) must survive -> pin-bump bot + fleet staleness census, D4 withdrawn; per-repo gates on GitHub Actions (free for public repos); cross-package tests atomized (step 0 minted as W318). mtools is already PUBLIC (gh repo view), so the split publishes nothing new | 2026-10-01: operator 2026-10-01: keep agents current via a meta package and/or >= floors set whenever something is built on a consumer's behalf. Plan takes both (floors = correctness, meta = freshness); both need real semver per module, so release publishing is decision D5 | 2026-10-01: operator 2026-10-01: D5 answered, PyPI with TestPyPI staging (stage -> TestPyPI dev builds, main -> PyPI gated on tests; Trusted Publishing); tests run on a self-hosted runner luthen-observability maintains (W319, with fork-PR fences) | 2026-10-01: operator 2026-10-01: org name 'mikemol_tools' (D1, spelling pending: GitHub allows no underscore; both hyphen and hyphenless forms unclaimed); D2 answered: each repo keeps its git history (git filter-repo per subdirectory) | 2026-10-01: operator 2026-10-01: D3 answered, mtools stays as the workstream repo. 'Tooling repo' was unclear: it meant the shared build and check machinery every module uses; proposed homing it as its own module repo instead | 2026-10-01: operator 2026-10-01: D1 mikemol-tools; shared machinery as its own modules with atomization and composition (W321 decomposes it). All operator decisions answered | 2026-10-01: org created by the operator: mikemol-tools at 2026-10-01T12:04:59Z, verified via gh (free plan, 0 public repos, operator admin/active, default permission read, 2FA requirement OFF). waypoints.title: bazel admits each ACTION before it materializes data into zram, letting running actions finish and zram's LRU GC drain between them
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Operator 2026-10-06 (replaces the watchdog/stop-a-running-job design): the key is an admission check prior to the executor copying data into zram, catching actions as they are about to begin; existing actions continue; zram's own GC cycle drains it LRU-style, so waiting for it to fall is sound (not a permanent pin). Measured on this bazel (bazel help build --long): no built-in dynamic per-action gate, but three native pieces. (1) --local_extra_resources=zram_mb=N plus target tag resources:zram_mb:X makes bazel's own scheduler queue an action until the resource frees (static N per command: size it from zram headroom at command start minus a margin; only tagged targets take part, so tag them in dist_checks/gate_stages). (2) --run_under (tests) and --shell_executable (shell actions) run a wrapper before each such action: wait there on the LIVE zram reading, with membudget's zram gate (W837) as the waiter. (3) --sandbox_base picks where per-action sandbox trees go. Not yet shown: a hook that gates every local action type dynamically (compile/py actions run through the sandbox binary, not a shell). Next: prototype (2) for tests and (1) for the heavy macro targets on mtools, measure whether the heavy zram writers are covered, and only then decide whether the remainder needs remote execution (remote_executor is already configured). Still open from the earlier measurement: the staged-tree wrapper path and adoption in the other bazel repos.

waypoints.title: A repo's gate reads an immutable snapshot of what it gates, never the live working tree: a tree object from a temporary index (git write-tree), materialized by git archive and gated there, so an edit mid-run cannot invalidate or poison a run

waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-07: OPERATOR RULING 2026-10-06: scratch paths are FIXED, period, and exposure to scratch space is NAMESPACED. So the snapshot lives at one fixed, namespaced path per repo (not a per-run mktemp, not a path that varies by sha), e.g. /var/tmp/mikemol/gate/<repo>/tree, which also keeps bazel's output base and analysis cache. One writer at a time by flock held for the whole run (the run reads a tree nothing can rewrite under it); the tree sha is stamped in the directory so a reader can tell which snapshot it is; the path is counted in the zram budget (project-zram1-real-limit). Anything else that wants scratch asks the same namespace for its own fixed path.

waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-07: 2026-10-07 measured on paperkit:W296. atomize-imports moved six function-level or re-export imports to module level in paper/checks/claims.py and six in paperkit/library/concepts.py. Those two files are dispatch-table modules (CLAIMS and CONCEPTS): tools/closure.py reads module-level imports as a BASE shared by every claim, so each claim's cone grew to the whole engine base, and the def-sweep fingerprints changed: the paper project's :cohere went red (two rests-on edges between compose claims reported disjoint, 2 of 83). Found by diffing per-claim closure roots, original file against rewritten: claims.py differed by 1 claim after removing the hoist (the function that lost its local import of gate), concepts.py differed by about 700 root rows until ten functions were given local imports; roots then equal the original exactly (diff empty) and the paper (111 claims) and library (43) gates pass locally. Why a function-local import must bring its siblings: import pkg.a inside a function binds pkg locally for the whole function, so every other pkg.b read there needs a local import before its first read (UnboundLocalError otherwise, measured on paperkit's project.py main). Workaround used: a scratch libcst script (host scratchpad localize_imports.py: remove the chosen module-level imports, add local imports of every module each reading function uses). Check to run after any atomize of a dispatch module: per-claim closure roots, old against new, must be equal except for the intended spelling changes.
